summary: Issue 8 — The Corporate Visit. Page 1: Arrival. The StarTrust Operations Liaison arrives as a competent professional who values the station's explicit unknowns.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Docking vestibule. The StarTrust Operations Liaison steps onto Stardust with one compact case and no entourage.
PANEL 2 — Astra meets them with Jax slightly behind, route slate in hand. LIAISON: I read the reports.
PANEL 3 — Astra gives the smallest professional smile. ASTRA: I'm sorry.
PANEL 4 — The Liaison almost smiles. LIAISON: I liked the parts that said "unknown."
PANEL 5 — Jax checks the first route clearance. JAX: Good. We have several more of those.

summary: Page 2: The Route. Jax demonstrates that his visitor-route ownership is real, documented, and subordinate to maintenance access.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax leads the Liaison through the operations level. The route is clean but visibly working, not staged.
PANEL 2 — They pass the properly racked passive-collection bins. LIAISON: Those were in the original installation location?
PANEL 3 — Jax shakes his head. JAX: Original location blocked maintenance access.
PANEL 4 — The Liaison notes it. LIAISON: Who authorized the move?
PANEL 5 — Jax raises the route slate. JAX: Local access override. Documented.
PANEL 6 — The Liaison nods. LIAISON: Good. Jax was prepared for a fight and does not get one.

summary: Page 3: No Demonstration. Astra states the central truth immediately: Stardust can show samples and tests, but cannot schedule the phenomenon.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra brings the Liaison into the lab work area where Mira has sealed samples and physical test records ready.
PANEL 2 — The Liaison sets down the case. LIAISON: Show me a production event.
PANEL 3 — Astra answers before Mira can. ASTRA: There isn't one.
PANEL 4 — The Liaison looks at her.
PANEL 5 — Astra continues. ASTRA: We can show you samples, conditions, tests, and chain of custody. We cannot schedule the phenomenon.
PANEL 6 — The Liaison nods once. LIAISON: Good. If you can stage it, I don't need a site visit.

summary: Page 4: What Can You Defend. Mira says 'None that we can defend' when asked for a reliable behavioral condition, and the liaison accepts the scientific limit.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira lays out the physical results from Issues 4–7.
PANEL 2 — The Liaison asks directly. LIAISON: What condition reliably produces high-cohesion material?
PANEL 3 — Mira does not look at Astra before answering. MIRA: None that we can defend.
PANEL 4 — The Liaison waits.
PANEL 5 — Mira adds. MIRA: We have physical context. We have samples with different properties. We do not have a predictive behavioral mechanism.
PANEL 6 — The Liaison writes exactly that down. LIAISON: Better than a false one.

summary: Page 5: The Reporting System. Glorp and Kreeb demonstrate that full material traceability and intentional personal blanks can coexist.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp presents the local reporting workflow.
PANEL 2 — Glorp points to the required sample fields. GLORP: Material traceability is complete from collection through test.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb points to the intentional blank category. KREEB: Personal disclosure is not required to complete the record.
PANEL 4 — The Liaison looks at NO ENTRY — INTENTIONAL BLANK. LIAISON: This created review questions.
PANEL 5 — Glorp visibly braces. GLORP: We can answer questions.
PANEL 6 — Kreeb looks at Glorp, pleased but not sentimental. KREEB: Yes.

summary: Page 6: The Tempting Question. The liaison acknowledges Stardust's procurement need and asks Astra only for a claim the liaison can honestly sign.
settingText: Observation-glass alcove off Stardust Station's working operations level; bright maintained corporate-station interior with the active lab visible nearby.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The Liaison asks Astra to step aside near the observation glass.
PANEL 2 — LIAISON: Your station needs procurement priority.
PANEL 3 — Astra glances toward the still-temporary bracket status. ASTRA: Yes.
PANEL 4 — LIAISON: A material pilot is easier to fund than "interesting operations."
PANEL 5 — Astra looks back at the lab. ASTRA: I know.
PANEL 6 — The Liaison does not threaten her. LIAISON: Then tell me what I can put my name on.

summary: Page 7: Ordinary Work. A mundane galley-water problem interrupts the tour and Astra stops trying to route the visitor around reality.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The tour resumes through the galley service corridor.
PANEL 2 — A station alert sounds: GALLEY WATER MANIFOLD — PRESSURE LOW.
PANEL 3 — Zib stops mid-step. ZIB: That's new.
PANEL 4 — Astra automatically begins to redirect the Liaison away. ASTRA: We can continue upstairs.
PANEL 5 — The Liaison looks at the alert. LIAISON: Is this part of the tour?
PANEL 6 — Astra gives up on the instinct to smooth it. ASTRA: It is now.

summary: Page 8: Route Changes. Jax independently closes the unsafe route and opens a bypass, performing the responsibility he volunteered for.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax checks the planned visitor path. The low-pressure manifold is directly ahead.
PANEL 2 — He closes that route segment and opens a safe bypass on his slate.
PANEL 3 — A worker starts to enter the service area. JAX: Not through here. Use the blue corridor.
PANEL 4 — The Liaison watches him enforce the detour without asking Astra.
PANEL 5 — Jax looks back at the Liaison. JAX: Route changed. LIAISON: I noticed.

summary: Page 9: The Failure. The actual problem is a sticking regulator actuator affecting one sink, and the crew treats it as exactly that size of problem.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib opens the manifold service cabinet.
PANEL 2 — Mira checks the sensor history. MIRA: Pressure drop started four minutes ago.
PANEL 3 — Zib finds a sticking regulator actuator. ZIB: There.
PANEL 4 — Astra asks the operational question. ASTRA: Isolation?
PANEL 5 — Zib points to the secondary galley branch. ZIB: We lose one sink. Nobody dies of thirst.
PANEL 6 — Station system announcement: GALLEY SINK TWO TEMPORARILY UNAVAILABLE. The Liaison watches the crew treat this as exactly the size of problem it is.

summary: Page 10: Work While Observed. The incident response is distributed across roles; Astra does not centrally direct every action.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib isolates the affected branch.
PANEL 2 — Jax keeps the service path clear and updates the route slate.
PANEL 3 — Mira compares commanded and actual actuator position. MIRA: Command is clean. Response is lagging.
PANEL 4 — Zib removes the actuator cover. ZIB: Because it is dirty.
PANEL 5 — Pixa logs elapsed response time and affected service count. PIXA: One fixture unavailable. No other service impact.
PANEL 6 — The Liaison asks Astra quietly. LIAISON: Who is directing this? Astra watches the crew. ASTRA: Depends which part.

summary: Page 11: No Hero. The liaison sees a whole repair response happen through distributed competence rather than one heroic command.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib cleans the actuator track.
PANEL 2 — Mira verifies sensor response.
PANEL 3 — Jax prevents a supply cart from entering the open service zone.
PANEL 4 — Astra handles the station notice and galley user complaints.
PANEL 5 — Glorp logs the temporary isolation while Kreeb puts a simple sign on the unavailable sink.

PANEL 6 — The Liaison sees the whole response happen without a central heroic command. LIAISON: You distribute incidents quickly. ASTRA: We distribute everything quickly. Usually because no one has enough hands.

summary: Page 12: Repair Closed. The ordinary incident ends in eleven minutes forty-two seconds, producing a measurable operations record rather than a heroic set piece.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib cycles the actuator.
PANEL 2 — Pressure returns to normal.
PANEL 3 — Mira confirms the trend. MIRA: Stable.
PANEL 4 — Jax reopens the route segment. JAX: Blue corridor released.
PANEL 5 — Pixa reports. PIXA: Total service interruption: eleven minutes, forty-two seconds.
PANEL 6 — Zib closes the cabinet. ZIB: Long because we had a tour. The Liaison accepts the hit.

summary: Page 13: The Sample. Residue is collected only after the repair; Mira explicitly refuses to attribute it to disagreement or any other behavioral recipe.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — After the repair, Mira notices a small incidental residue seam near a warm cable junction beside the service cabinet.
PANEL 2 — She waits until the area is closed and safe before sampling it.
PANEL 3 — The Liaison watches. LIAISON: Was that caused by the disagreement?
PANEL 4 — Mira looks at them. MIRA: No behavioral recipe.
PANEL 5 — The Liaison clarifies. LIAISON: Then what caused it?
PANEL 6 — Mira seals the sample. MIRA: We do not know.

summary: Page 14: What Repeats. The liaison recognizes that the reproducible pattern is the station's incident response, not the material yield.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Back in the lab, the Liaison compares two sets of records: material samples and operational incidents.
PANEL 2 — Material side: LOW MASS / VARIABLE PROPERTIES / NO DEFENSIBLE PREDICTOR.
PANEL 3 — Operations side: INCIDENT DETECTION / LOCAL OWNERSHIP / SERVICE ISOLATION / REPAIR CLOSURE.
PANEL 4 — The Liaison points to the second list. LIAISON: This repeats.
PANEL 5 — Astra sees what they mean. ASTRA: The failures?
PANEL 6 — The Liaison shakes their head. LIAISON: The response.

summary: Page 15: Issue One Comes Back. The released Issue 1 inspection result becomes evidence that adaptive response has been Stardust's repeatable value from the beginning.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra pulls the old inspection result from Issue 1.
PANEL 2 — The inspector's conclusion is visible: STATION REMAINS ACTIVE — ADAPTIVE RESPONSE ACCEPTABLE.
PANEL 3 — The Liaison reads it. LIAISON: Same pattern.
PANEL 4 — Astra looks slightly embarrassed by the phrase. ASTRA: We thought that was a polite way to say "messy but useful."
PANEL 5 — The Liaison returns the file. LIAISON: It can be both.
PANEL 6 — Brick, from the edge of the room: BRICK: The old witness returns. Nobody engages him.

summary: Page 16: Change the Pitch. Astra removes unsupported yield language and replaces it with measurable operations plus passive material characterization.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra has her original material-pilot talking points open.
PANEL 2 — She deletes: POTENTIAL YIELD / SCALE PATH / PRODUCTION CONDITIONS.
PANEL 3 — She replaces them with: UPTIME / RESPONSE TIME / LOCAL OWNERSHIP / PASSIVE MATERIAL CHARACTERIZATION.
PANEL 4 — Mira watches. MIRA: That's a different pitch.
PANEL 5 — Astra answers without looking away from the screen. ASTRA: It's a different station.
PANEL 6 — Mira corrects her. MIRA: Same station. Astra looks at her. ASTRA: Right.

summary: Page 17: The Question. Astra explicitly refuses to sell certainty the station does not have; the liaison tells her to sell the operating record instead.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The Liaison closes their case.
PANEL 2 — LIAISON: I can recommend a limited pilot. Central review will ask what it produces.
PANEL 3 — Astra looks at the sample tray, then the operations record.
PANEL 4 — ASTRA: I am not selling certainty we do not have.
PANEL 5 — The Liaison nods toward the operations record. LIAISON: Then sell the operating record.

summary: Page 18: Terms. The local trial terms preserve passive collection, scientific limits, consent, chain of custody, and no output target from the liaison.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra, Mira, Glorp, Kreeb, and the Liaison write the local trial terms.
PANEL 2 — Astra states the first term. ASTRA: Passive collection only.
PANEL 3 — Mira states the second. MIRA: No behavioral conditions.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb adds. KREEB: No personal disclosure required.
PANEL 5 — Glorp adds. GLORP: Material chain of custody remains complete.
PANEL 6 — The Liaison adds the last local term. LIAISON: No output target from me. Astra notices the qualifier.

summary: Page 19: What Central Will See. The liaison submits the adaptive-operations framing but warns that central finance may still generate a material benchmark.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The Liaison shows Astra the recommendation form before submitting it.
PANEL 2 — Program description: ADAPTIVE OPERATIONS SITE WITH INCIDENTAL MATERIAL CHARACTERIZATION.
PANEL 3 — Astra reads it twice. ASTRA: That is almost a sentence I recognize.
PANEL 4 — The Liaison points at the review note. LIAISON: Central finance may still ask for a material benchmark.
PANEL 5 — Astra looks at them. ASTRA: You said no target.
PANEL 6 — The Liaison is precise. LIAISON: I said no target from me.

summary: Page 20: Jax Closes the Route. The liaison validates Jax's route work as actual incident handling, not merely tour support.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The visit is ending. Jax walks the Liaison back toward docking.
PANEL 2 — He checks off the final route segment.
PANEL 3 — The Liaison hands back the temporary visitor badge. LIAISON: Route was clear.
PANEL 4 — Jax looks at the badge. JAX: We had one unscheduled detour.
PANEL 5 — The Liaison gestures toward the repaired galley corridor. LIAISON: You handled it.
PANEL 6 — Jax puts the badge in the return slot. JAX: That was the route.

summary: Page 21: Recommendation Sent. The competent human visit ends well, but Astra knows the larger system still gets a vote.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The Liaison departs.
PANEL 2 — Astra's terminal receives: SITE RECOMMENDATION SUBMITTED.
PANEL 3 — Mira stands beside her. MIRA: That went better than I expected.
PANEL 4 — Astra does not celebrate yet. ASTRA: A person visited. The system still gets a vote.
PANEL 5 — Pixa chimes. PIXA: Central review acknowledgement received.
PANEL 6 — Astra looks at the new attachment. ASTRA: There it is.

summary: Page 22: Tag — Target Mass. Central review—not the liaison—extrapolates one visit-day sample into a material benchmark, causing Issue 9.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Close on the central review message: LIMITED PILOT — PROVISIONAL.
PANEL 2 — Second line: MATERIAL BENCHMARK GENERATED FROM OBSERVED SITE DATA.
PANEL 3 — Third line, larger: TARGET MASS UPDATED.
PANEL 4 — Mira reads the number and immediately frowns. MIRA: They extrapolated the visit sample.
PANEL 5 — Astra looks at the target, then at the still-open operating record. ASTRA: Of course they did.
